title: Towers & Columns
summary: Custom fabricated industrial process towers and columns with specified internals, materials, mechanical design and transport segmentation requirements.
body:
Tongyang fabricates industrial process towers and columns to approved drawings and project specifications. Column geometry, material selection, internals interfaces and fabrication sequence are reviewed alongside the mechanical design basis and delivery constraints. For large equipment, transport envelope and shipment segmentation should be evaluated early in the project.

Types of process towers and columns

  • Distillation columns: fabricated column shells and specified internal interfaces for separation processes
  • Absorption and stripping towers: equipment for gas-liquid contacting duties defined by the process design
  • Gas treatment columns: shells and mechanical interfaces for specified treatment and separation services
  • Tray or packed columns: with tray supports, packing supports, distributors and other internals where specified
  • Large column sections: shop-fabricated modules or transport sections for site assembly where project logistics require them

Industries and applications

  • Chemical and petrochemical plants
  • Oil and gas processing and gas treatment
  • Distillation, absorption and stripping services
  • Industrial separation and mass-transfer processes
  • Projects requiring large fabricated shells and coordinated site interfaces

Key technical parameters for quotation

  • Geometry: internal diameter, tangent-to-tangent height, total height, head type and overall dimensions
  • Mechanical design: operating/design pressure, vacuum conditions, design temperature, wind and seismic loads, material and corrosion allowance
  • Column internals: tray or packing arrangement, support rings, distributors, manways, attachments and internal drawings
  • Connections and supports: nozzle schedule, skirt or support details, insulation, lifting and erection points
  • Fabrication and quality: welding requirements, NDE, dimensional tolerances, pressure testing and documentation
  • Transport and installation: road/port transport envelope, maximum section dimensions and weight, shipment split, site weld scope and erection interfaces

Fabrication, design codes and quality

Plate forming, shell fabrication, welding, inspection and dimensional control are planned against the approved drawings and project specification. The applicable mechanical design code may include ASME Section VIII, GB/T 150 or another agreed code, as applicable to the equipment and project. Certification, inspection and conformity requirements are confirmed separately for the destination market and contractual scope.

Process design, mass-transfer calculations, tray or packing performance and separation guarantees remain the responsibility of the appointed process-design party unless these services are expressly included in the agreed scope. Internals fabrication and installation responsibilities must also be clearly defined.

Heavy fabrication capabilities

Shop resources relevant to large tower and column fabrication include plate rolling capacity up to 120 mm, CNC cutting capacity up to 80 mm and lifting capacity up to 200 tonnes. These are facility equipment limits, not guaranteed limits for every finished column. Feasibility for a specific diameter, shell thickness, section length and unit weight is confirmed through engineering, workshop handling and transport reviews.

Where required by transport restrictions, columns may be evaluated for fabrication and shipment in multiple sections. The number and length of sections, field-circumferential welds, NDE access, lifting points and site assembly responsibilities must be agreed in the project execution plan.

Transport planning for large columns

For tall or large-diameter columns, transportation can affect the fabrication split, field welding, inspection access, lifting arrangement and total project cost. Please provide the delivery destination, available transport limits and site assembly constraints as early as possible. Any proposed shipment split must be checked against structural design, welding procedures, inspection requirements and the approved erection plan.

Related equipment

Columns are often integrated with associated thermal and separation equipment. Explore our heat exchangers, condensers and reboilers and pressure vessels and process drums for related equipment categories.

Preparing a tower or column RFQ

For an initial review, provide the process and mechanical data sheets, general arrangement drawing, column internals drawings, design conditions, materials, applicable code, inspection requirements and destination. For oversized equipment, include transport limits and any preference for shop shipment in sections versus site assembly.

Quotation basis: final fabrication scope, internals, shipment segmentation, site welding, installation, inspection, certification and delivery schedule are confirmed against the approved project documents.
